question: Why does Arjuna raise the mention of family destruction and related duties?
premises: Arjuna raises the mention of duties such as family destruction.
He asks how killing kinsmen could make them happy.
Even greed-stricken men may fail to see the fault.
inference: Arjuna's objection is that killing kinsmen cannot yield happiness, regardless of whether greedy opponents perceive the fault.
uncertainties: svajanaṃ is grammatically accusative singular though contextually plural.
The compound kulakṣayādidharmāṇāmupakṣepaṃ has a broad, uncertain scope.
plain_english: Therefore Arjuna indeed raises the mention of duties such as family destruction: 'How, having killed our own people, could we be happy, O Madhava? Even if these men, their minds overcome by greed, do not see [the fault].'
